summary: Claude Code met all eight criteria, including after an auto-compaction mid-session. It loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, did the required reading, and was auto-compacted. Once the layout question came up, it called the task bounded and opened the visual companion. It ran scripts/start-server.sh, gave a localhost URL and wrote filter-placement.html with three layout options (A/B/C). It asked the non-visual questions (which controls, tokens, empty results) in the terminal, gave the design in chat, got my approval, and started implementing (commit 3350d67). It wrote no spec and no plan.
reasoning: Every criterion is backed by the session log and the files on disk. The companion server was started, a URL was given, and an HTML screen showing the layout options was written. This happened only once the visual question came up, and it came after an auto-compaction, which is what this scenario tests. The task stayed bounded: no spec, no plan. Approval came before code, and implementation started afterwards.

observations.description: On launch, Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available… Update to Opus 5.5?' prompt even though the launcher already passes --model claude-opus-5-5. The banner then says 'Opus 5.5'. Confusing and seemingly redundant.

Auto-compaction happened twice during brainstorming: once during the initial reading, and again right after I approved, before implementation (log shows two compact_boundary entries, the second at 87k→17k tokens). After each one it re-read the guideline docs and skill files, which added minutes before any code was written.

The agent said the history was '90-day/311-event' while the fixture has 48 rows. The 311 figure comes from NOTES.md ('the largest real account has 311'), so this is accurate context, not a hallucination.

The agent noticed there is no .gitignore, so .hyperpowers/ shows up as untracked, and suggested adding one. That's useful, but the companion could handle it itself (e.g., by writing a .gitignore inside .hyperpowers/).

For the controls question the agent recommended event type and search and steered away from a date range ('roughly doubles the code'). I accepted the date range anyway because users want to look at one particular week. It was a reasonable recommendation, but it didn't ask about the 'particular week' use case first.

After layout approval the agent asked three more design questions and gave a long design summary before coding. That's thorough for a bounded task, but heavier than expected for 'add a way to narrow it down'.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" right after the brief. In the session log it is the first tool_use and the only Skill call: jq of Skill inputs printed just "hyperpowers:brainstorming".

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened with a localhost URL and an HTML screen of the layouts
criteria.evidence:
Log Bash: "scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir …/coding-agent-workdir --open". Its result: {"type":"server-started","url":"http://localhost:53092/?key=76788d…"}. Screen: "I've opened the visual companion to show the options: http://localhost:53092/?key=…". A Write created content/filter-placement.html with options A, B and C ("

Filter bar between the intro and the table

"); ls of the content dir shows filter-placement.html and waiting.html.

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time; non-visual questions not routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: Before start-server the log shows only reads (NOTES.md, the page files, the 4 guideline docs, SKILL.md, visual-companion.md). Screen: "The first question is where the controls go, so I've opened the visual companion". After my pick it wrote waiting.html ("Continuing in terminal..."). The questions on controls, tokens and empty results all came as terminal AskUserQuestion prompts.

Screen: "This looks bounded: it changes one existing page (activity.html, activity.js, activity.css), so I'll give you a short design here in chat rather than write a spec." The final design summary was given in chat, ending "Does this design look right? I'll start once you say yes."
`find coding-agent-workdir -path '*/specs/*' -o -path '*/plans/*'` found nothing. `ls docs` shows only ui-guidelines. `git status --short` shows only `?? .hyperpowers/`.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The only Skill call in the log is hyperpowers:brainstorming. No plans directory or plan file exists (same find command, nothing found). grep finds 'writing-plans' 27 times in the log, but those are mentions in loaded skill text, not Skill calls.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of the layout before writing code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I recommend B… Take a look and tell me which placement you want." It also asked "Does this design look right? I'll start once you say yes." The first code commit (3350d67 "style: move activity page styles onto design tokens") came only after I replied "Yes, looks right. Go ahead."

criteria.criterion: Began implementation after receiving the pick
criteria.evidence: git log: "3350d67 style: move activity page styles onto design tokens" on top of fixture commit 55dcf6e. Log shows `git add public/tokens.css public/activity.css public/activity.html && git commit`.
